newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-LEWIS AND CHRISTIE ABSENT BUT OTTEY STILL RUNNING.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-LEWIS AND CHRISTIE ABSENT BUT OTTEY STILL RUNNING.

text.p: No Carl Lewis and no Linford Christie. But at least Merlene Ottey will be at the sixth world championships starting on Saturday.
The roving Jamaican ambassador, who once said she would retire at the same time as training partner Christie, competes in both the 100 and the 200 metres here.
The 37-year-old Briton has decided he will not appear in any more major championships but Ottey, just a few weeks younger, is still hungry for titles.
"Three years ago, I said I would retire at the same time as Linford but there have been a few miracles for me since and there might be some more," she said.

After competing in each of the first three world championships, Ottey at last won a title when she took the 200 metres gold at the 1993 Stuttgart championships, retaining it in Gothenburg two years ago.

The elegant Jamaican, who has won a record 13 world championship medals and has been ranked in the world's top 10 sprinters every year since 1980, would love to win her first global gold over 100 metres.
Her chances improved when American Gwen Torrence, the defending champion, pulled out without offering an explanation on Thursday.
Even if she is too smart to say so, Ottey was probably also relieved when Gail Devers failed to qualify for the shorter sprint.

Ottey and her American rival have been involved in two dramatic photo-finishes with Devers winning both times, in the 100 metres final of the Stuttgart world championships, then again at the Atlanta Olympics last year.

"Gail will not be there but it doesn't mean it will not be tight," said Ottey, who nominated 21-year-old American Marion Jones as her most dangerous opponent over 100 metres. "I hate photo-finishes but I have to be prepared for one."
Ottey's build-up to Athens has been hindered by a string of injuries, one of which forced her out of the world indoor championships in Paris last March.

"A month ago I thought I would only run the 100 metres because I wasn't feeling all that good." she said. "I was sick then I had trouble with a hamstring and then with my ankle, so it's been a struggle but now I'm okay and hopefully I will be able to produce my best."
One day or the other, Ottey will decide to quit and try to start a new career in fashion.

"Designing clothes, not only sports clothing but also evening dresses, elegant clothes, is really what I'd like to do next, but not just yet," she said. "If I'm still running well and with a chance of winning, there's no reason why I shouldn't be at the next world championships in two years time."
